title: Surge moderation bridge and async-circuit rewind
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Backfills a new surge moderation bridge that coordinates soft tenant evictions during cross-region surge and adds an async circuit-state rewind to avoid noisy rapid reopen cycles.
description:
Context: During a cross-region capacity surge incident on 2024-12-28 we observed rapid circuit flips and noisy tenant reopen events causing cascading evictions and increased tail latency for best-effort workloads. This PR implements a 'surge moderation bridge' that sits between the SLO enforcer and the regional circuit manager and introduces an async circuit-state rewind path to prevent immediate reopen attempts after a soft-eviction window.

Motivation: reduce oscillation in circuit state and give regional autoscaler time to react without hard-evicting tenants, improving end-user latency and reducing overall token spend during incidents.

Summary of changes and checklist:
- Add a new coordination component: surge-moderation-bridge service with lightweight RPC between slo-enforcer and circuit-manager.
- Implement async circuit-state rewind: persist a minimal circuit snapshot to local DB and schedule a background reconcile that will attempt reopen only after a decayed, heuristically-computed cooldown.
- Introduce tenant tethering: a soft-quarantine token that de-prioritizes requests but allows progressive probe traffic for warmup.
- Expose new metrics: surge_bridge.active_windows, circuit_rewind.attempts, tenant_tether.count, tenant_probe.success_ratio.
- Integrate with regional autoscaler signals: added hooks to prefer gradual capacity increases instead of immediate full reopen.
- Tests: unit tests for cooldown heuristics, e2e test via perf-canary scenario, and documented runbook steps.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear (ENG-5243) [x] unit tests added and passing locally [x] perf canary validated with synthetic spike [x] telemetry dashboards updated [x] rollout steps recorded in runbook [x] security review of RPC (mTLS) completed

- Flaky test: tests/perf/canary/surge_probe.yml had intermittent timing; added increased timeout and retry in canary harness.

Rollout plan and canary:
- Feature gated behind feature flag: surge_moderation_bridge.enabled=false by default.
- Step 1 (canary): enable for 1% of traffic in us-west-2 for 2 hours; monitor surge_bridge.active_windows and tenant_probe.success_ratio.
- Step 2: expand to 10% for 6 hours if metrics stable.
- Step 3: full rollout across regions with staged ramp if no regressions.

Runbook highlights (from docs/runbooks/surge-moderation.md):
- Abort criteria: sustained increase in 95p latency > 15% or tenant_probe.success_ratio < 0.9 for more than 10 minutes.
- Immediate rollback: flip feature flag to false and trigger circuit-manager forced-stable state.
- Emergency mitigation: if oscillation persists, toggle slo-enforcer to emergency-mode which will prefer immediate hard reopens (last-resort).

Observability and metrics:
- New Prometheus metrics added and Grafana panels created.
- Added tracing spans around bridge RPC and rewind attempts.
- Logs include structured event "surge_bridge.window_opened" and "circuit_rewind.attempt_scheduled".

Security/ops considerations:
- RPCs are mTLS-authenticated and audited; documented in infra/README.
- Surge bridge runs in its own K8s namespace and uses RBAC minimal privileges.

Post-merge actions and follow-ups:
- ENG-5389: tune cooldown parameters per workload class based on 2-week canary data.
- ENG-5410: A/B compare cost delta with/without tenant tethering.
- Add a dashboard alert for frequent rewind attempts (>5 per 5m) to detect oscillation.

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash on 2025-01-22 by Aisha Patel after approvals from all reviewers.

Why this is different from previous approaches: Instead of hard immediate reopen or aggressive eviction, the bridge coordinates a staged, telemetry-backed decision and uses an async rewind to avoid noisy reopen cycles — focusing on smoothing transitions and giving autoscaling time to provision capacity.

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: all behavior is behind a feature flag and default parameters are set to be close to current production heuristics. The intent is to reduce incident blast radius while preserving the ability to rapidly recover once capacity has stabilized.
